newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Some tobacco company options busy.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Some tobacco company options busy.

text.p: A few tobacco company options were active Thursday as the group fell on anticipation of a settlement between Liggett Group and several state attorneys general.
The American Stock Exchange's Tobacco Index of nine companies was down 6.53 points, or 2.25 percent, at 283.92 in afternoon trading, above its 281.52 session low.
Industry giant Philip Morris Cos Inc led the group, dropping 7-1/8 to 114-7/8. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp dipped 5/8 to 31-5/8. But Brooke Group Ltd, which owns Liggett, added 5/8 to 4-7/8.
Several Philip Morris options were active, particularly in the expiring March series, but action was steady in the April, June and September expiration months also.

But a couple of Philip Morris LEAPS (long term equity anticipation securities) were the most active, as the January 1998 130 call traded nearly 5,300 contracts and the January 1998 150 call traded about 4,215.
The January 130 calls, which had open interest of 2,301 contracts, were trading at 8-1/8, down 1-5/8, and the January 150 calls were down 7/8 at 3-3/4. Its open interest was 1,687 contracts.
Michael Schwartz, managing director at Oppenheimer & Co, said the volume, most of which was done as a spread, was likely from an investor putting on a bull LEAP spread.
"The best way to be in this -- because of the uncertainty -- is to have a spread," he said. "So they could be replacing some of their position in the stock."
The investor putting on the spread paid roughly $5 for the chance to make a profit of $15, making an attractive risk/reward profile, Schwartz said.
"It's aggressive because of the choice of strike prices," said Gregory Nie, a technical analyst at EVEREN Securities. "Somebody is saying the stock will come back."
Philip Morris shares peaked out at 139-3/4 on March 11 and have been in a steady downtrend since, but Nie said the stock's longer term uptrend remains unbroken.
"The long term trend is still intact," he said. "If anything, the stock is probably going to weaken a little further.
"I wouldn't rule out a retest of 106, which was a previous breakout level," he said.
Nie added that the stock was overextended on its quick run to the 140 area and the news background has provided an excuse for profit taking that was overdue.
He said RJR Nabisco's retreat from its 38-7/8 late February high simply put it back in the middle of a long term trading range, with downside support likely in the upper 20's.

The American Stock Exchange began trading options on the TOB March 5 and despite the action in the underlying stocks, just 103 contracts traded, the most being 25 of the March 320 puts. The April 305 and May 320 calls each traded 10 contracts and the April 320 call traded 20.
